All seven study points and an additional initialization control converged.
Independent review supports the bounded result and transport-scaling implementation;
it does not establish a general-purpose initialization capability. No manuscript
files have been edited.
Rendering never runs the model.

## Question and conditions

How do ±10% changes in liquid viscosity, liquid free-CO₂ diffusivity and the
liquid-side CO₂ transfer coefficient affect capture and peak liquid temperature
in the manuscript's nonisothermal Case 3C? These are exploratory correlation
sensitivities, not measured uncertainty intervals or a joint uncertainty model.

The model is read directly from the manuscript task's `bad5` checkout, without
editing its files: nine-species reactive ePC-SAFT bulk equilibrium, neutral-vapor
closure and conventional enhancement-factor film, with the existing empirical
caloric and transport correlations. This is not the separate full reactive-film
study or an eNRTL comparison.

The feed table supplies liquid flow 2.08805556 kg/s, reported dry gas flow
0.55916667 kg/s, lean loading 0.25 mol CO₂/mol MEA, unloaded MEA mass fraction
0.30, dry CO₂/O₂ fractions 0.093/0.090, gas temperature 316.75 K, and pressure
109500 Pa. Lean temperature 318.15 K is an imputed input, as marked in that
table, not a newly verified measurement. Dry saturated vapor conversion,
packing, effective-area correlation, kinetics and caloric inputs are held fixed.

Engine commit: `9e1bef97fbea5c6f465612ae27b054192f91f19c`.
Wheel SHA-256: `b011d0f9d492e9db197f67cc0ae6781ac636fa3278805ddf1d6a05ecd167074b`.
Evaluated parameter fingerprint:
`sha256:07e3f93b209d8e117af4b69e2d0ab3b5bc0b2e94568643c28629e4799d8aa062`.
The installed-wheel final-integration check passed; see
[the retained check](figures/response/input/engine_check.txt).
Each run retains the parameter and reaction documents and input/source hashes.

The supplied column Jacobian combines native thermodynamic derivatives with
differentiated absorber equations. All runs use 41 initial nodes, residual
tolerance 0.05, boundary tolerance 0.001 and at most 1000 nodes, matching the
manuscript's refined reference.
Reported temperature peaks are maxima on the common 101-position exported
profile, using the same definition as the manuscript reference.

| Perturbed input | Multipliers | Dependencies recalculated |
|---|---|---|
| Liquid-mixture viscosity, Pa s | 0.9 and 1.1 | Ionic diffusion, holdup, liquid transfer, gas transfer through holdup, enhancement and heat transfer |
| Liquid free-CO₂ diffusivity, m²/s | 0.9 and 1.1 | Liquid transfer, Hatta number and enhancement; MEA and ion diffusivities are not directly scaled |
| Liquid-side CO₂ coefficient, m/s | 0.9 and 1.1 | Hatta number, enhancement and combined film resistance; scaling precedes these evaluations |

Vapor viscosity and diffusivity are not directly perturbed. Because the three
perturbations share physical dependencies, their responses must not be combined
as independent statistical uncertainties.
In this model, ionic diffusivity varies as liquid viscosity to the power −0.7;
the separate CO₂ and MEA diffusivity correlations are not directly functions of
viscosity. The viscosity screen preserves that distinction.

## Baseline verification

The fresh unit-multiplier column converged in two mesh iterations to 42 nodes,
with capture **91.5483865996%**, maximum normalized residual **0.0431384383**
and zero maximum scaled boundary residual. Its capture differs from the
manuscript's retained refined result by **−0.0000000227 percentage points**.
Three model files have changed since the retained initialization run; the wheel,
parameter bundle and physical settings match. The new factor-one result is the
baseline for the transport comparisons.

All six perturbed assembled column-RHS directional-derivative checks passed using
the manuscript's existing independent check at one seven-state test point per
multiplier. This is not an independent derivative audit at every axial position.
Centered differences verify the Jacobian here; they never construct the
production solver Jacobian.
See [derivative_checks.json](figures/response/output/derivative_checks.json).

## Column response

![Case 3C capture and peak liquid-temperature changes under separate ±10% transport multipliers. Points are completed simulations, not a fitted response curve. Shading shows the magnitude of the previous joint mesh/tolerance change; it is not an uncertainty interval.](figures/response/output/transport_sensitivity.png){#fig-transport}

| Input | Multiplier | Capture (%) | Capture change (percentage points) | Peak liquid temperature (K) | Peak-temperature change (K) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Baseline | 1.0 | 91.548387 | 0 | 347.861545 | 0 |
| Liquid viscosity | 0.9 | 91.830465 | +0.282078 | 347.878178 | +0.016633 |
| Liquid viscosity | 1.1 | 91.256147 | −0.292240 | 347.840313 | −0.021233 |
| Liquid CO₂ diffusivity | 0.9 | 91.630866 | +0.082479 | 347.866071 | +0.004526 |
| Liquid CO₂ diffusivity | 1.1 | 91.455059 | −0.093328 | 347.855017 | −0.006529 |
| Liquid-side CO₂ coefficient | 0.9 | 91.017015 | −0.531371 | 347.824975 | −0.036570 |
| Liquid-side CO₂ coefficient | 1.1 | 91.946512 | +0.398125 | 347.879041 | +0.017496 |

The numerical authority is [summary.csv](figures/response/output/summary.csv);
[profiles.csv](figures/response/output/profiles.csv) retains axial responses,
transport values and effective conductances. Extra displayed digits make the
comparison reproducible, not an assertion of corresponding physical accuracy.

For equal relative perturbations, capture responds most to the liquid-side
coefficient, then viscosity, then CO₂ diffusivity. The tested capture range is
**91.017–91.947%**, versus **91.548%** at baseline. Every capture change exceeds
the previous 0.00510-percentage-point refinement change. This establishes a
resolved local transport response for this case, not a probabilistic uncertainty
range or a ranking under measured input uncertainties.

Increasing CO₂ diffusivity does not simply increase capture in the adopted
enhancement-factor model: it changes both physical transfer and enhancement.
For the +10% run, the median ratio at corresponding axial positions is
approximately **1.047** for the liquid coefficient and **0.931** for enhancement;
their product has a median ratio of **0.975**. These are recoupled profile
comparisons, not fixed-state derivatives. They support interpreting the small
negative capture response through the combined film closure rather than
assuming proportionality to diffusivity. This sign is conditional on that
closure and is not asserted as a general property of reactive absorption.

All computed peak-temperature changes are within **0.037 K**, below the
previous **0.04493 K** refinement change. The study therefore does not establish
the sign or ordering of these small thermal responses as numerically resolved.

### Numerical evidence

All seven points converged in two mesh iterations to 42 nodes. Maximum
normalized residuals span **0.04270–0.04354**, below the common 0.05 stopping
tolerance; maximum scaled boundary residuals are zero. Accepted runs report no
invalid-state penalties or failed/best-effort equilibrium states. Maximum axial
CO₂ and water flow-balance variations are **2.23×10⁻¹⁵** and **4.27×10⁻¹⁴ mol/s**;
maximum species-balance and charge discrepancies are **1.51×10⁻¹¹** and
**2.65×10⁻¹⁵ mol/s**, respectively.

Net enthalpy-flow variation is **272.08–273.14 W**, approximately **6.1×10⁻⁵**
relative to its profile magnitude. It is retained as a numerical diagnostic,
not reported as exact energy conservation. Each run retains its full result,
profiles, parameter/reaction documents and source identities.

## Diagnosed initialization failure

The first −10% diffusivity run and its instrumented repetition failed in a cold
equilibrium initialization at **323.8714530382 K and 109500 Pa**. The failing
state was the loading-path anchor (CO₂/MEA = 0.25), not an accepted column
result. The Engine reported numerical nonconvergence without adjudicating
physical feasibility.

A direct probe reproduced the cold-start failure. A certified neighbor 0.01 K
higher then initialized convergence at the **exact original temperature**, and
subsequently at the exact requested column composition. Both exact states had
native derivatives available and passed local stability checks. The requested
column state had liquid density **51114.8520963 mol/m³** and CO₂ fugacity
**1302.3693696 Pa**. This identifies an initialization failure, not an
inadmissible thermodynamic state or failure of the transport formulation.

Changing only the initial column profile passed the first failed trial but
encountered the same cold-start issue during mesh refinement at
323.8714274963 K. The second exact state also converged after warm initialization.
The completed calculation supplies the certified anchor composition as an
equilibrium starting guess, conservatively mapped to the requested feed by the
model's existing helper. Every requested state is still solved and certified
at its own temperature, pressure and composition. Physical inputs, equations,
transport multiplier and stopping tolerances are unchanged. The direct probe
establishes state-only feasibility; the completed column separately exercises
the unchanged production loading-continuation path. No failed trial is replaced
by a penalty or counted as a converged result.
See [the exact failure trace](figures/response/output/diffusivity_090_diagnostic/failure_trace.json)
and [direct probes](figures/response/output/diffusivity_090_diagnostic/state_probe.json).
The [profile-only retry](figures/response/output/diffusivity_090_reinitialized/failure_trace.json)
and [its exact-state probes](figures/response/output/diffusivity_090_reinitialized/state_probe.json)
are retained separately.

The factor-one control and −10% diffusivity run each used 11 supplied cold-anchor
starting guesses. The control changed capture by **1.01×10⁻¹¹ percentage points**,
peak liquid temperature by **1.20×10⁻¹² K**, and the liquid-temperature profile
by at most **5.53×10⁻¹¹ K**. This checks that the starting-guess change did not
shift the baseline result. See [initialization_control.csv](figures/response/output/initialization_control.csv)
and the completed run's [initialization record](figures/response/output/diffusivity_090_seeded/initialization.json).
It does not establish general cold-start reliability for the Engine.
The starting-profile and anchor inputs are verified for these retained runs;
the diagnostic helper is not validated for arbitrary external seed files.

## Interpretation limits

The manuscript's previous joint mesh/tolerance refinement changed capture by
approximately **0.00510 percentage points** and peak liquid temperature by
**0.04493 K**. These are resolution indicators, not certified error bounds.
Small responses cannot establish temperature insensitivity below that
resolution. One operating case cannot establish plant-wide uncertainty,
correlation accuracy or general cold-start reliability.

For reviewer R1.9, the supported contribution is a direct column-level
transport sensitivity study with the current manuscript thermodynamics:
capture changes by at most 0.532 percentage points in the specified screen,
whereas the smaller temperature responses remain below the previous refinement
change. This complements, but does not replace, source/applicability discussion
for the correlations, the thermodynamic-parameter study, or operating-condition
sensitivity. It does not cover gas-side correlation uncertainty, interfacial
area, kinetics, caloric inputs, correlated errors or other operating cases.

## Numerical sensitivity: interfacial-area coefficients (issue 84)

Chinen et al. (2018), supporting information, Table S3, PDF page 3
(Zotero parent `KJ688HMG`, attachment `6WCMFD9H`, SHA-256
`f9591338c28337502f8525c4b72b26fcd99ad7b3aaa05aa20c2e6db51be74081`),
reports fitted Tsai-form coefficients $A_1=1.42$ and $A_2=0.12$. The table also
lists typical literature values of 1.34 and 0.12; Tsai's 2010 dissertation
(`KQSWX5T9`, printed p. 142, Eq. 6.10) gives 1.34 and 0.116. Chinen's
article, sections 2 and 3.2.5, describes a simultaneous mass-transfer and
kinetics parameter regression using Dugas wetted-wall data and Tobiesen packed-tower data
for Mellapak 250Y, selected as structurally similar to the intended
MellapakPlus 252Y. It is not a standalone area-only fit.
The 3C input tuple uses 250 m²/m³ and 0.97 void fraction, matching the
repository's named MellapakPlus 252Y configuration; that tuple alone does not
establish the physical packing identity. The case 3C operating record is the
published 2017 input described in `analyses/bvp_solution_methods/input/case_3c.json`.

Both runs within each route use identical inputs and settings, with only the
pair in the area expression changed in memory. The form includes the existing
void fraction. The twelve-state case uses solved-state hydraulic density, 11
cosine-upwind nodes, five quadrature points and tolerance $10^{-7}$. The
seven-state case uses ideal Henry equilibrium, adaptive collocation and its
default residual tolerance 0.5. Temperatures and area ranges are evaluated at
native nodes. Capture is the percentage of inlet vapor CO2 removed.

| Route | Pair | Capture (%) | Effective area (m²/m³) | Peak liquid temperature (K) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Seven-state Henry | Chinen 1.42, 0.12 | 90.417 | 226.956–230.864 | 348.668 |
| Seven-state Henry | Tsai 1.34, 0.116 | 89.918 | 217.397–220.994 | 348.586 |
| Twelve-state conserved | Chinen 1.42, 0.12 | 90.024 | 225.395–228.392 | 342.609 |
| Twelve-state conserved | Tsai 1.34, 0.116 | 89.343 | 215.953–218.692 | 342.418 |

The Tsai pair lowers capture by 0.499 and 0.681 percentage points respectively
on these specified bases. These are model predictions for a controlled numerical
sensitivity, not physical validation or an estimate of uncertainty. The
seven-state solves reported convergence with maximum RMS residuals 0.048 and
0.031 at tolerance 0.5; the retained attempt records numerical acceptance as
not evaluated. The twelve-state cases pass their native-grid material, energy,
charge, interface and boundary checks, with maximum scaled residuals
$7.29\times10^{-9}$ and $3.45\times10^{-9}$. Eleven nodes do not establish
between-node accuracy. The twelve-state loaded density reads about 11% high
against Amundsen 2009, reducing 3C holdup by about 12–16% (issue 83); the
thermal reference remains provisional. No coefficient adoption decision follows
from this comparison alone.

[Requests, attempts, diagnostics and logs](results/runs/tsai_area/) are
retained. The first seven-state attempts used the default single-shooting
method and were interrupted after it ran much longer than expected; the
completed seven-state calculations use the existing `scipy-bvp` method. The
analysis-only [substitution](scripts/tsai_area/sitecustomize.py) is inherited
by the isolated worker; the production default is unchanged. Run `compare.py`
with `ISSUE84_PAIR` and its directory on `PYTHONPATH` as shown in the retained
requests, then `summarize.py` for seven-state node quantities. These results
have not been independently reviewed or promoted for manuscript use.

From the repository root, use a fresh output label or remove only the prior
analysis output after preserving it, then run each combination (`seven` or
`twelve`, `chinen` or `tsai`) with the corresponding pair:

```bash
ISSUE84_PAIR=1.42,0.12 PYTHONPATH="$PWD/analyses/transport_sensitivity/scripts/tsai_area:$PWD/src" \
  nice -n 10 uv run --frozen python analyses/transport_sensitivity/scripts/tsai_area/compare.py twelve chinen
ISSUE84_PAIR=1.34,0.116 PYTHONPATH="$PWD/analyses/transport_sensitivity/scripts/tsai_area:$PWD/src" \
  nice -n 10 uv run --frozen python analyses/transport_sensitivity/scripts/tsai_area/compare.py twelve tsai
uv run --frozen python analyses/transport_sensitivity/scripts/tsai_area/summarize.py
```

Replace `twelve` with `seven` for the corresponding seven-state cases. For the
current pair, an independent symbolic evaluation of the analysis expression
and its density derivative agreed with the production expression at
$\rho_L=1000$ kg/m³. This check verifies the substitution at that point, not
column mesh convergence.
